thesis: The currency of this deck is a Dinosaur ENTERING the battlefield, not a creature attacking: Gishath's combat-damage reveal manufactures entries in batches (goldfish, 10,000 games: the reveal fired in 7,300 games, 2.016 times a game, for 4.08 free bodies), and V5 rebuilt the layer that cashes them — Purphoros turns every entry into 2 damage at each seat and Molten Echoes turns every nontoken Dinosaur entry into a second one, so a deck that used to need its 7/6 to keep connecting now has a payoff layer that pays without a combat step.

stages.label: THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB
stages.what_it_does: Pays for a commander whose mana value is 8 and whose modal card in the 99 costs 3 (deck-audit: curve modal mana value 3). 35 land copies across 24 entries here, plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, two land sorceries, Mirari's Wake and five creatures that make or fix mana. deck-audit reads mana-base 35 copies against a 36-38 target and mana-sources 42 against a floor of 42 — the base is one land light and exactly on the source floor. V5's land pass shows up in the tapland count: 4 copies enter tapped unconditionally (deck-audit taplands 4, target <= 8; mana_analysis enters_tapped 10, always 4). Colour, not quantity, is the strain, and V5 moved it the wrong way: mana_analysis reads W 19 / R 21 / G 30 sources and on-curve probability with rocks and dorks W 0.866, R 0.610, G 0.822 — red is the worst colour, and the two cards V5 added to the conversion layer are Purphoros at {3}{R} and Molten Echoes at {2}{R}{R}. Regal Behemoth and Wayward Swordtooth are filed here rather than among the Dinosaurs because what they do for this engine is mana and a land drop; Bloom Tender's Vivid mana scales with the colours already on board, which in this deck arrive late. Measured: 'Ramp or fixing drawn' assembles in 91.0% of games, 74.3% by turn 6, mean turn 3.106, over a nine-card group that is 49.8% of opening sevens.

stages.label: THE FIRST CONNECTION
stages.what_it_does: The thing everything else waits on: Gishath resolves, attacks, and connects once. He prints his own vigilance, trample and haste, so the kit's job is not to let him attack — it is to make the hit land and to make the reveal WIDE, because the number of cards revealed is his power. Rogue's Passage ({4}: unblockable) and Kessig Wolf Run (+X/+0) are lands and survive a wrath; Kinjalli's Sunwing makes opponents' creatures enter tapped, which strips the flashed-in blocker; Sunfrill Imitator may copy him while attacking, and because the copy's name stays Sunfrill Imitator the legend rule does not apply — that is a second reveal trigger and it is UNVERIFIED. Three cost reducers shrink the cast itself, a command-zone cast being a cast: Otepec {1} less, Urza's Incubator {2} less on the chosen type, Knight of the Stampede {2} less. All three are generic-only, so the floor is {R}{G}{W}. A fourth door exists and is not here: Hunting Velociraptor (fuel) gives Dinosaur spells prowl {2}{R}, which by its oracle text should apply to Gishath from the command zone — but only AFTER a Dinosaur has connected, so it is a re-cast discount, not a first-cast one, and it is unverified. Measured: the commander's mean cast turn is 7.278, median 7, and only 26.7% of games cast him by turn 6 — this is the pinch in the deck. 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' assembles 83.0%, 65.4% by turn 6; 'The Gishath connection kit' 81.1%, 61.2% by turn 6. The connect rate itself is FORGE'S, not the model's: 0.70 per attack, and the goldfish has no blockers.

evidence.note: one 7-damage connection resolved by the checker: four simultaneous entries, three Uprising draws, one Pantlaza discover at X=6

stages.label: WHAT THE TOP OF THE LIBRARY HOLDS
stages.what_it_does: The reveal converts only what is on top, so this layer buys arrangement and extra entries rather than named cards. Congregation at Dawn stacks three creatures at instant speed, Worldly Tutor one; Enlightened Tutor finds Molten Echoes, Urza's Incubator, Mirari's Wake or Descendants' Path. The free-entry doors skip the cast entirely: Descendants' Path each upkeep, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, Huatli's Saga, Savage Order (which searches a Dinosaur straight onto the battlefield and is the only card in the 99 that sacrifices a CREATURE — six fetches and two Sagas sacrifice themselves and nothing else does, which is why this deck has no `fodder` stage at all). World War Hulk's chapter I is a free red or green creature spell, and its later chapters feed the ignition stage instead. Hunting Velociraptor is the new one worth reading carefully: prowl {2}{R} on every Dinosaur spell you cast AFTER a Dinosaur has connected, which is a cost reducer that only exists once the engine has already fired. Up the Beanstalk draws on every spell of mana value 5 or greater. The audit is blunt about the layer: card-advantage reads 6 copies against a floor of 10, with Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Rishkar's Expertise, Runic Armasaur and Vaultborn Tyrant named as doing the job uncounted, and the goldfish models 3 of 9 draw cards (draw_not_modelled: Curious Altisaur, Hunter's Insight, Jetmir's Garden, Runic Armasaur, Selvala and Vaultborn Tyrant), so every draw figure here is a floor.
cards: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

evidence.note: A role is a property, not an interaction, and this one scatters: of the four cards carrying draw:engine, only Up the Beanstalk is in this stage — Curious Altisaur and Garruk's Uprising are conversion and Selvala is mana. deck-facts also reports that card_roles.json has no pattern at all for Hunter's Insight, Rishkar's Expertise or Descendants' Path, so the count on this stage is a floor.

stages.label: WHAT AN ENTRY IS WORTH
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper, and the half V5 rebuilt. Every card here reads an ENTRY and pays something: Pantlaza discovers X = the entering creature's toughness, once a turn; Garruk's Uprising and Vaultborn Tyrant draw on each power-4-or-greater entry; Earthshaker Dreadmaw draws for each other Dinosaur as it arrives; Regisaur Alpha adds a 3/3; Curious Altisaur and Quartzwood Crasher price the swing instead. The two new ones change what the stage produces. Purphoros converts an entry into DAMAGE — 2 to each opponent for every other creature that enters, your side untouched — and it reads tokens too, so Regisaur Alpha's 3/3 and Ghalta and Mavren's attack tokens pay as well as the reveal's bodies. Molten Echoes converts an entry into a second entry: name Dinosaur, and every NONTOKEN Dinosaur you control that enters makes a hasty copy exiled at the next end step. I enumerated the copy's value from cards.json rather than assuming it: 10 Dinosaurs in the deck carry an entry trigger, 8 of them fire on the token copy, and Zacama and Wakening Sun's Avatar do not, both being gated on 'if you cast it'. Separately, 7 of the 29 Dinosaur cards are legendary, so their copy dies to the legend rule at once — the trigger still resolves, the body does not stay. Trapjaw Tyrant and Wrathful Raptors convert DAMAGE dealt to your own Dinosaurs instead, which is why the protection stage feeds them. Measured: 'Dinosaur payoff drawn' 85.6%, 61.5% by turn 6 — over a six-card group that names neither Purphoros nor Molten Echoes.

evidence.note: Pantlaza and Garruk's Uprising both resolved off one wave of simultaneous entries, with the Regisaur token ordered last so it cannot re-trigger the once-a-turn discover
Wrathful Raptors converting damage dealt to your own Dinosaurs into damage at a player

The Molten Echoes enumeration, read card by card from cards.json rather than from the role tag. Ten Dinosaurs in the deck carry an entry trigger: Bronzebeak Foragers, Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Itzquinth, Pantlaza, Regal Behemoth, Regisaur Alpha, Trumpeting Carnosaur, Vaultborn Tyrant, Wakening Sun's Avatar and Zacama. Eight fire on a token copy; Wakening Sun's Avatar and Zacama do not, both being gated on 'if you cast it'. Three of the eight are legendary (Itzquinth, Pantlaza, Zacama), so the copy's trigger resolves and the body dies to the legend rule. The value:etb role itself misses Pantlaza and Vaultborn Tyrant, both of which have one.

stages.label: WHAT THE BOARD POINTS AT
stages.what_it_does: Removal, the one sweeper, and the damage that gets aimed at your own side on purpose. deck-audit reads interaction 9 copies against a floor of 8, sweepers 1 against 1-3, and interaction-breadth 3 classes against 5, naming graveyard and land as classes with no answer detected — the check is an oracle heuristic and a floor, but Beast Within left in V5 and with it the land answer. Blasphemous Act is the deck's single point of failure by deck-audit's own reckoning and the input to the one asymmetric sweep. Savage Stomp is the V5 addition that matters structurally: it costs {G} pointed at your own Dinosaur, puts a +1/+1 counter on it, and the fight marks damage on YOUR creature — which is an enrage trigger and, under Temple Altisaur, exactly 1 damage taken. I enumerated every card in the 99 that can mark damage on your own Dinosaur without spending an answer on yourself: Blasphemous Act, Savage Stomp, Itzquinth (its damage may be aimed at another creature you control), Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode and Zacama's {2}{R}. The previous model said Blasphemous Act was the only one; that claim is now false. Wakening Sun's Avatar destroys all non-Dinosaurs but only if you CAST it from hand, so it is dead off the reveal and dead off Molten Echoes — the same clause that stops Zacama untapping your lands.

evidence.note: Blasphemous Act cast for {R} off nine creatures; state-based actions clear the opponents' creatures before the redirects choose targets

stages.label: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER
stages.what_it_does: Insurance on a plan that is entirely one creature. Read them rather than count them: Heroic Intervention's hexproof and Akroma's Will's protection from each colour cover targeted exile and bounce; Boros Charm's indestructible covers a wrath but not an exile; Flawless Maneuver is the only one castable for nothing on the turn you tap out for eight; Eerie Interlude is the only one that dodges a non-targeted mass exile, and with the V5 conversion layer down it is no longer only a dodge — the end-step return is a simultaneous entry of your whole board, which is Purphoros damage at every seat and a Molten Echoes copy of every nontoken Dinosaur. Temple Altisaur is prevention rather than a body: 'if a source would deal damage to another Dinosaur you control, prevent all but 1', which is what makes Blasphemous Act one-sided and what turns Savage Stomp's fight into a 1-damage enrage trigger. It is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, so the Act kills it, and stack 004 resolves that exact sequence. Measured: 'Protection held for the board' assembles 71.7%, 52.2% by turn 6, over a five-card group that is 31.2% of opening sevens; deck-audit reads protection 8 copies against a 5-7 target and calls it OVER.

evidence.note: Temple Altisaur prevents all but 1 to every other Dinosaur and takes 13 itself

stages.label: THE TRAMPLE SWING, AND THE OTHER ONE
stages.what_it_does: The games this deck wins, it wins by attacking with more power than three seats can block: goldfish mean board power reaches 34.415 at turn 8, kill-by-turn-8 is 0.609 and the mean kill turn is 7.987 in a model with no blockers, which makes those a ceiling on speed and a floor on nothing. Overwhelming Stampede is the finisher and also an ignition card in disguise — +X/+X where X is the greatest power among your creatures makes Gishath's reveal that many cards wider. Ghalta and Mavren is the other half: its attack trigger makes tokens, and a token entering is a Purphoros trigger, so the swing now pays before blockers are declared. Ghalta, Primal Hunger costs {X} less for the total power you control, so ten power on board makes a {G}{G} 12/12; Regal Imperiosaur is an anthem for other Dinosaurs; Carnage Tyrant is the body that answers counterspells and targeted removal by itself; Pugnacious Hammerskull is a 6/6 for three that stuns itself only while it is your only Dinosaur, which in this deck is an early problem and never a late one. The second kill route is the one V5 installed and it does not live in this stage: Purphoros needs no combat step at all, and every entry the reveal, the tokens and Molten Echoes produce is damage at all three seats.

evidence.note: The taxonomy's wincon:combat role belongs to Akroma's Will, Boros Charm and Huatli in this deck — none of them here — and it has NO entry at all for Overwhelming Stampede, which is the stage's finisher. Five of the 99 carry no role (deck-facts).

map_disagreements.why: Purphoros is filed in Insurance with the protection spells and the cost reducers, because four of its five lines are 'indestructible', 'devotion', 'isn't a creature' and a +1/+0 pump; the single clause that earns its slot — 2 damage to each opponent per entry — is outvoted by its own card text. Molten Echoes lands in Bodies with the creatures, which is right for the wrong reason: it makes bodies, but its job is multiplying TRIGGERS. Trapjaw Tyrant sits in Interaction and Wrathful Raptors in Bodies although they are the same enrage converter. No clustering over oracle text can see that all eleven of these cards read the same event.

engine-facts' scatter puts 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' across 4 cities and 'The Gishath connection kit' across 3. Gishath clusters with the Dinosaurs, his three cost reducers with Blasphemous Act on 'costs {N} less', and his evasion with the lands. Nothing in any card's text says 'these make one attack happen'; the connection is a board event, which is exactly what a text clustering cannot represent.

Five cities for one job. Mana and Mana II split on a text feature with no functional content — fetches say 'search your library', everything else says 'add' — while Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim are filed with the TUTORS for the same phrase, and Regal Behemoth and Wayward Swordtooth read as Dinosaurs because that is what their type line says. A creature that makes mana is filed as a creature.

map_disagreements.component: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER (protection)
map_disagreements.why: Temple Altisaur is the prevention effect stack 004 turns on, and the map files it among the Dinosaurs, because it is a 4/5 whose ability is written as a replacement effect rather than as a protection keyword. Eerie Interlude is in Bodies too, on 'return those cards to the battlefield'. The four instants that say 'gain hexproof / indestructible / protection' are in Insurance; the two that do the same job without the vocabulary are not.

open_questions.question: Does Sunfrill Imitator, attacking beside Gishath and copying him, give a second combat-damage reveal — and does the legend rule leave both on the battlefield, given the copy's name stays Sunfrill Imitator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would be the only way in the 99 to double the reveal in one combat, and the whole deck is throughput per connect. If it works, the Imitator stops being a 3/3 filler card and becomes ignition; if the legend rule bites, it is a trap.

open_questions.question: With Hunting Velociraptor on the battlefield and a Dinosaur having dealt combat damage to a player this turn, may Gishath be cast FROM THE COMMAND ZONE for his prowl cost of {2}{R} plus the commander tax?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The binding constraint on this deck is the commander's cast turn — mean 7.278, 26.7% of games by turn 6 — and the second and third casts carry the tax on top. If prowl is a legal alternative cost from the command zone, a three-mana Gishath re-cast after a removal spell is the largest single change V5 made to the deck's floor, and it is currently modelled nowhere: the goldfish reads Velociraptor on the bodies and combat channels only.

open_questions.question: On a board with Gishath connecting for 7, Purphoros and Molten Echoes both out, what is the exact damage to each opponent and the exact order of the entry triggers — specifically whether each Echoes copy's own entry re-triggers Purphoros, and whether Pantlaza's once-a-turn discover can be pointed at a copy rather than the original.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the V5 thesis in one board state. The whole claim that the deck now kills without combat rests on the count of Purphoros triggers per connect, and nothing has resolved it.

open_questions.question: Does the goldfish's reveal channel feed the ETB layer — do Purphoros' fixed damage and Molten Echoes' copy fire off the bodies the declared commander reveal puts onto the battlefield, or only off cards cast from hand?
open_questions.why_it_matters: model-coverage reports Purphoros and Molten Echoes as `seen` on the bodies/combat channels, but `seen` means a channel is switched on, not that the reveal's entries route through it. If they do not, every damage figure for V5 is measuring the pre-V5 deck.

open_questions.question: Is Wakening Sun's Avatar still worth a slot now that the deck's entries mostly arrive off the reveal and off Molten Echoes, both of which turn its ETB off ('if you cast it from your hand')?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's second sweeper on paper and a 7/7 vanilla in the engine's own lines, at {5}{W}{W}{W} against W 0.866 on-curve for a single pip — triple white is a different question.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Purphoros, God of the Forge, Molten Echoes, Vaultborn Tyrant and Earthshaker Dreadmaw to the any_of group, and move Descendants' Path out of it into the cost-reducer/cheat group where it already appears.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The group is the deck's per-entry payoff layer and it currently names six cards, none of which is either card V5 added to that layer. deck-audit already names Vaultborn Tyrant and Earthshaker Dreadmaw as doing an uncounted job on the card-advantage axis. Descendants' Path is a free-cast DOOR, not a payoff, and counting it in both places is what lets the payoff figure read high.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: The Gishath connection kit (haste or evasion for the 7/6)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Drop Regisaur Alpha, Otepec Huntmaster and Knight of the Stampede; keep Rogue's Passage, Kessig Wolf Run and Overwhelming Stampede, and add Kinjalli's Sunwing and Mirari's Wake.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Gishath prints his own haste, so the two haste grants in the group cannot help him connect and Knight of the Stampede grants nothing at all toward it — three of the six members measure something the commander already has. What the group should measure is evasion and REVEAL WIDTH, since the number of cards revealed is his power; Mirari's Wake and Overwhelming Stampede both raise it.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Split into two targets: 'Command-zone discount drawn' (Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator, Knight of the Stampede, and Hunting Velociraptor if the prowl question resolves yes) and 'Cheat-into-play door drawn' (Descendants' Path, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People, Savage Order, World War Hulk).
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Only the first three can reduce a command-zone cast, and the commander's cast turn is the deck's binding constraint (mean 7.278, 26.7% by turn 6). A seven-card group in which four members cannot touch the pinch reads 83.0% assembled and tells the pilot nothing about whether the discount is there. This edit was proposed against the V4 list and is still unapplied.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Mark `required: true` on 'Ramp or fixing drawn' and on no other target.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Among the DRAWN components this is the only one the deck cannot function without: everything else is a payoff that matters only after Gishath resolves and connects, and Gishath himself is in the command zone, so the true single point of failure cannot be a goldfish target at all. Two cautions the pilot should weigh before applying it: the group assembles in 91.0% of games, so the split is close to degenerate, and CLAUDE.md records that engine-lift figures computed from authored `required` flags were deleted on 2026-08-28 because three defensible declarations of one deck gave contradictory signs.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either add the damage SOURCES (Savage Stomp, Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath, Triumphant Chomp, Zacama, Primal Calamity) as a second any_of clause, or retire the target.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: As declared it names only the two converters, Trapjaw Tyrant and Wrathful Raptors, which convert nothing on their own — they need damage marked on your own Dinosaurs. V5 added a cheap repeatable source (Savage Stomp, {G} at a Dinosaur), which is the first time the residue has had an enabler that is not a board wipe. The target currently measures half a mechanism and reads 58.4%.
